title: The Architecture of Weightlessness: Why Python Standard Library Beats 800MB Node Modules
author: Jeremy Lee
excerpt: Modern web tools routinely pull thousands of transitive dependencies just to generate static HTML. Here is why Kaze returns to first principles.
body:
Modern web development has developed a dependency addiction. To produce a dozen static HTML files, typical toolchains pull 800+ nested npm packages, spin up a multi-gigabyte Node.js runtime, and spend 45 to 90 seconds compiling on CI.

### The Standard Library Advantage

Python has shipped with a world-class standard library for decades. Everything required to compile a static website is already present:

1. **Filesystem Traversal:** The `os` and `shutil` modules handle directory mirroring and asset copying with zero overhead.
2. **Structured Content:** The `json` module parses configuration and data models natively in microseconds.
3. **Sanitization and Escaping:** The `html` module provides secure HTML entity escaping without third-party sanitizers.
4. **Text Transformation:** The `re` module delivers industrial-grade regular expression performance for markdown parsing and token interpolation.

### Instant Compilation: 0.01s Benchmark

Because Kaze has zero external packages to resolve, parse, or type-check, compilation executes in roughly 10 milliseconds. On a standard VPS or Cloudflare Pages build worker, `python3 build.py` finishes before the shell prompt can even render its status bar.

### Long-Term Maintenance Immunity

When you build with zero external pip dependencies, your project cannot break due to an abandoned package or an incompatible minor version bump. A Kaze repository written today will run identically ten years from now on any machine with Python 3.

faq.q: Does Kaze require any pip packages?
faq.a: No. Kaze relies 100% on the Python 3 standard library. You do not need to create a virtualenv or run pip install.
A standard multi-page marketing site with blog articles, case studies, and templates compiles in approximately 0.01 seconds.
